description: Rule by which the platform suggests a bias-correction method for each cycle, target and product (scripts/bias_recommend.py, docs/47). Fixed before the independent validation seasons are scored. A suggestion is advice for a decision; it never changes the published forecast.
historical: A method is a candidate only if the confirmation (CHIRPS, outer leave-one-year-out over the training years, full pipeline) finds it better than the operational method with Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05 (false discovery rate) across every declared method and target, and not worse over the test years. Variants outside the declared family are not candidates.

changes.note: Decided by the project lead after the sensitivity analyses (33-year and pooled evidence, Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg) had been seen; the decisions are recomputed from the p-values each benchmark stored, within the same families. The benchmarks keep their own Holm decisions as run.

choice: Among candidates, the method the selection-aware procedure chooses from all training years (training-only information); if that method is not a candidate, the candidate with the best training-period score. Other candidates are listed as alternatives: a confirmation establishes improvement against the operational method, not a ranking among candidates.

validation.rule: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py). A candidate is 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the operational method, and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer seasons it stays a 'candidate'; with enough seasons and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'.

statuses.keep: Keep the operational method: no method is confirmed better on the historical evidence.
statuses.candidate: Confirmed better on the historical evidence; independent validation seasons are still being collected.
statuses.recommended: Confirmed better on the historical evidence and not worse over the independent validation seasons.
statuses.not_supported: Confirmed better on the historical evidence but worse over the independent validation seasons.
